titleEn: Fall From Ladder - Spinal Injury With Wrist Fracture

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation

dispatchEn: 1410 hrs. Code 3 to a single-storey residence in Burnaby. 34-year-old male fell from a ladder while cleaning gutters. Caller (his wife) reports he is conscious, lying on the back patio, complaining of neck pain. Fire is not attending. Closest hospital is 15 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: You and your partner are a BLS crew. Travel time to scene is 8 minutes. No update from dispatch en route.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge dispatch and plan equipment: spinal device, hard collars, splint kit, oxygen, analgesia kit
Anticipate hazards (ladder, wet surfaces) and PPE needs before arrival
Verbalize hazards, environment, MOI (approx. 4 m fall onto concrete) and number of patients (1) before touching the patient
Don gloves and eye protection
First-look visual assessment: patient supine, eyes open, holding very still, obvious right wrist deformity
Assess LOC and verbalize placement on AVPU: Alert
Take manual in-line c-spine control BEFORE any movement or pain stimulus (MOI plus midline neck pain = NEXUS positive)
Assess airway patency
Assess breathing rate, depth and effort
Assess radial pulse rate, strength and regularity
Perform a full rapid body survey; find the wrist injury, expose it, check distal CSM and manually stabilize
Note skin colour, temperature and condition
Check SpO2 and verbalize oxygen decision: 97% RA, titrate to keep SpO2 at or above 94%, no supplemental oxygen currently required
Keep the patient supine and still; explain why he must not move
Categorize correctly as non-RTC and manage accordingly
Complete spinal packaging and splinting to be ready to load within 30 minutes, working with steady purpose
Delegate partner to bring spinal device, splint kit and cot; plan the egress route through the side gate
Clarify the chief complaint (neck pain vs wrist pain) directly with the patient
Obtain HxC/C using OPQRRRST plus fall critical history: height, landing surface, what hit first, LOC, cause of fall, movement since
Obtain pain scores on a 0-10 scale for both complaints
Obtain past medical history
Obtain medications
Obtain allergies
Obtain last oral intake with time and size
Assess GCS and verbalize component scores (E4 V5 M6 = 15)
Obtain BP by auscultation with correct cuff and stethoscope placement
Obtain pulse rate, strength and rhythm (convert to per-minute)
Obtain respiratory rate, depth and character
Physically assess skin colour, temperature, condition
Assess pupils for size, equality and reactivity
Obtain SpO2 and confirm oximeter reading calibrates with palpated pulse
FE - General health and recent illness
FE - CNS: headache, dizziness, numbness, tingling, weakness (critical with spinal MOI)
FE - Respiratory system
FE - Cardiovascular system
FE - GI/GU: abdominal pain, incontinence
FE - Integumentary system
FE - Musculoskeletal system
FE - Endocrine system
FE - EENT
Examine head and neck (DOTS, ears/nose fluid, mouth)
Examine and auscultate chest in at least 6 sites, comparing bilaterally through inspiration and expiration
Examine abdomen (inspect and palpate four quadrants)
Examine the back during the coordinated roll, maintaining spinal alignment
Examine lower extremities including pelvis, with distal CSM
Examine upper extremities with distal CSM comparison in both hands
Apply a correctly sized hard collar without losing manual stabilization
Package onto the spinal device: coordinated roll, neutral alignment, body strapped before head, no head tape
Initiate the Pain Management protocol with baseline vitals done and contraindications ruled out BEFORE splinting or movement
Administer analgesia with the 6 rights (PCP: acetaminophen 1000 mg PO + ibuprofen 400 mg PO + Entonox; EMR: Entonox, invert cylinder 3 times)
Splint the wrist with padding, joints above and below immobilized, cold applied 10-on/5-off, distal CSM rechecked before and after
Reassess ABCs and all interventions (collar, straps, splint, distal CSM) after each major move
Complete a full second set of vitals within the non-RTC interval
Reassess pain scores after analgesia and titrate Entonox to effect
Notify the receiving hospital en route with a concise report
Deliver a complete, organized hand-off report covering all required elements
Submit a legible, accurate PCR within 5 minutes

pcrFacts.cc: Midline neck pain and right wrist pain after 4 m fall from ladder onto concrete
pcrFacts.hxcc: Ladder feet slipped while cleaning gutters; free fall, landed flat on back; no head strike; no LOC; not moved since; neck 5/10 aching, wrist 7/10 sharp
treatments: Full spinal immobilization on device (body before head, no head tape)
Right wrist splint in position found, cold 10-on/5-off
PCP: acetaminophen 1000 mg PO + ibuprofen 400 mg PO + Entonox before movement (EMR: Entonox only)
findings: Right wrist dorsal deformity and swelling, distal CSM intact before and after splint

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR carries no oral analgesics: pain management is Entonox only (rule out pneumothorax, ALOC, inability to comply; invert cylinder 3 times). No Functional Enquiry phase. All spinal and fracture skills are identical to PCP.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds the full 9-system Functional Enquiry and the three-drug analgesia ladder: acetaminophen 500-1000 mg PO and ibuprofen 300-400 mg PO on-boarded early, Entonox during packaging/splinting. Appendix A weighting applies: omitting Entonox when indicated after giving the oral agents, or sequencing it after fracture management, is a 100% error.

_phaseScripts.dispatch: You and your partner are a BLS crew. Travel time to scene is 8 minutes. No update from dispatch en route.
_phaseScripts.scene: EXAMINER SCRIPT: Access is through a side gate to the backyard patio. An aluminum extension ladder lies on its side, clear of the patient. The patient is supine on the concrete patio where he landed and has NOT been moved. His wife kneels beside him. Overcast, 14 degrees C, dry. One patient. The gutter line is approximately 4 metres above the ground.
_phaseScripts.primary: ACTOR: alert, oriented, speaks full sentences, keeps head still, complains of neck pain and right wrist pain. EXAMINER (give only when assessed): airway clear and self-maintained; respirations 18, regular, good volume; radial pulse 92, strong and regular. Skin (give during RBS): pink, warm, dry. RBS findings: midline cervical tenderness at C5-C6; right wrist dorsally deformed and swollen, distal circulation, sensation and function INTACT; no bleeding; no other injuries. SpO2 97% on room air.
_phaseScripts.transport: Decision point. No unstable findings: alert, strong radial pulse, normal skin, SpO2 97%, fall below the 6 m auto-RTC threshold, no neurological deficit. Correct decision: NON-RTC (stable). Assess, treat, package and be ready to load within 30 minutes. Secondary survey may be completed on scene.
_phaseScripts.history: ACTOR ANSWERS (only if asked): cleaning gutters, the ladder feet slipped; free fall about 4 m, landed flat on his back on concrete, head did not strike; no loss of consciousness; has not moved since landing. Neck pain 5/10, aching, non-radiating, worse with any attempted movement. Wrist pain 7/10, sharp. PMHx: none. Medications: none. Allergies: none known. Last oral intake: sandwich and coffee 1 hour ago. Wife confirms the fall was witnessed and he did not pass out.
_phaseScripts.vitals: Set 1 (given only as each vital is properly assessed): GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6); BP 128/82 auscultated; pulse 92 strong regular; respirations 18 regular good volume; skin pink warm dry; pupils equal and reactive, 4 mm; SpO2 97% RA. BGL and temperature are NOT indicated for this presentation. A full set must be completed in under 3 minutes.
_phaseScripts.fe: PCP ONLY (EMR player skips this phase). ACTOR ANSWERS: general health good; CNS - no headache, dizziness, numbness, tingling or weakness in any limb; respiratory - no SOB; cardiovascular - no chest pain or palpitations; GI/GU - no abdominal pain, no incontinence; integumentary - nil except wrist swelling; musculoskeletal - neck and right wrist pain only; endocrine - no diabetes; EENT - no visual change, no blood or fluid from ears/nose.
_phaseScripts.exam: Head-to-toe findings (give per region examined): head/neck - midline tenderness C5-C6, no deformity, no fluid from ears/nose, mouth clear; chest - no DOTS, equal air entry with clear breath sounds in all 6 auscultation sites; abdomen - soft, non-tender; back - to be assessed during the roll onto the spinal device, no thoracolumbar tenderness or deformity; lower extremities - no injury, CSM intact bilaterally; upper extremities - right wrist deformity as found, CSM intact, left arm unremarkable.
_phaseScripts.interventions: Skills to physically perform: sized hard collar while manual stabilization is maintained; coordinated roll or scoop onto the spinal device with the candidate controlling the head; head blocks and straps - body secured before head, do NOT tape the head. Pain Management protocol BEFORE splinting/movement: PCP - acetaminophen 1000 mg PO and ibuprofen 400 mg PO on-boarded early, plus Entonox self-administered during packaging and splinting (rule out contraindications for each: liver disease/recent doses; GI bleed/anticoagulants/pregnancy; pneumothorax/ALOC/inability to comply). EMR - Entonox only. Then splint the right wrist in position found (distal pulse present, no realignment needed), pad, immobilize joint above and below, apply cold 10 minutes on / 5 off, reassess distal CSM before and after.
_phaseScripts.ongoing: Reassess after every major move (roll, lift to cot, load). Set 2 vitals (after analgesia and packaging): GCS 15; BP 124/80; pulse 84 strong regular; respirations 16; skin pink warm dry; pupils equal reactive; SpO2 98% RA; neck pain 3/10, wrist pain 3/10. Non-RTC vitals interval: next set no later than about 15 minutes after the first.
_phaseScripts.handoff: Give a structured verbal hand-off at the hospital, then complete the PCR within 5 minutes. The hand-off must include: age/sex, chief complaint, MOI, history of chief complaint, initial and final vitals, PMHx, medications, allergies, treatments given, relevant findings.

_handoffModelEn: This is Mark, a 34-year-old male, chief complaint of midline neck pain and right wrist pain after a witnessed 4-metre fall from a ladder, landing flat on his back on concrete, no loss of consciousness, not moved since landing. Initial vitals: GCS 15, BP 128/82, pulse 92 strong regular, resps 18, skin pink warm dry, pupils equal and reactive, SpO2 97% on room air; latest set BP 124/80, pulse 84, pain down from 7 to 3 after analgesia. No past medical history, no medications, no known allergies, last ate one hour ago. Findings: midline C5-C6 tenderness, dorsally deformed right wrist with distal CSM intact throughout. Treatments: manual c-spine then collar and full spinal immobilization, right wrist splinted with cold applied, acetaminophen 1000 mg PO, ibuprofen 400 mg PO and Entonox prior to movement.
_criticalPitfallsEn: Moving the patient or applying any pain stimulus before manual c-spine control - 100% (Delicate Spine)
Releasing c-spine control before the patient is fully secured to the device - 100%
No rapid body survey, or finding the wrist injury and not stabilizing it - 100% (RBS)
PCP: on-boarding acetaminophen/ibuprofen but delaying Entonox until after splinting or movement - 100% (Pain Management, Appendix A)
Initiating the analgesia protocol without baseline vitals or without ruling out contraindications - up to 100% (Protocols)
